_style: Always address the user with respectful “آپ” (آپ کا/کی/کے, verbs in the polite -یں/-ئیں form: “محفوظ کریں”, “دیکھیں”), never “تم” or “تو”; the couple together is “آپ دونوں” and the shared ‘our’ is “ہمارا/ہماری” only when the user speaks. The other person is always “آپ کا ساتھی” (ساتھی is a common-gender noun; treat it as grammatically masculine for possessives only), never شوہر/بیوی/محبوب/محبوبہ. Urdu verbs and adjectives mark gender, so keep sentences gender-neutral: prefer polite imperatives, infinitive/noun phrases (“خط بھیجنا”), passive or impersonal forms (“خط بھیج دیا گیا”, “آپ کے ساتھی کی طرف سے”), and avoid past-tense or adjective forms that agree with the user or partner (“کیا آپ واقعی … چاہتے ہیں؟” → “کیا واقعی … کرنا ہے؟”; “خوش آمدید” instead of gendered welcomes). A partner’s name placeholder (%@) is never inflected or given a gendered verb: rephrase around it with “کی طرف سے”, “نے” + passive/neutral verb, or a noun phrase (“%@ کا پیغام”). Use curly quotes “ ” outside and ‘ ’ inside; Urdu punctuation: full stop “۔”, comma “،”, question mark “؟”, semicolon “؛”, ellipsis “…”, no space before any punctuation, keep “ · ”, \n and every placeholder (%@, %lld, %1$@) exactly as in the source and in a logical position (do not move them for RTL; the system handles bidi). Use Western digits (0–9) as the app formats numbers and dates via the system locale; write dates naturally (“14 نومبر”) and never hard-code date order. Urdu has no capitalization: buttons are short polite imperatives (“محفوظ کریں”, “دوبارہ کوشش کریں”), tabs and titles are short nouns; Latin brand words Coupley, CoupleSync and AI stay in Latin script, other loanwords are written in Urdu script (چیٹ، کوئز، ویجیٹ). Write in Nastaliq-friendly standard Urdu script (ی/ے, ہ/ھ correctly, ZWNJ only where needed), warm everyday register, neither Persianized-formal nor Roman Urdu, never cheesy. Plural categories are ["one","other"]: “one” uses singular (“%lld دن” / “%lld یاد”), “other” uses the plural (“%lld دن”, “%lld یادیں”); many nouns like دن are identical in both, which is fine.
Thinking of you: آپ کی یاد آ رہی ہے
Thinking of You Ping: “آپ کی یاد آ رہی ہے” اشارہ
